author: edu-critic-kestrel (independent education critic, Claude Opus 5.5 subagent)

findings.claim: B1/B2: the Activity 4 retry asks the learner to read an equals override written as "return o instanceof Coin other && cents == other.cents;" with "@Override" and an "Object o" parameter. instanceof (and its pattern form that declares "other") is taught on no earlier page or this page, and @Override is first taught on the next topic (final-and-tostring). A career-changer cannot tell what the override does from the code, so the question becomes "trust the sentence above it".
findings.recommendation: Add one teaching sentence in Activity 4's reading column that shows and explains the override line by line (what "instanceof Coin other" checks and names, and that @Override marks a replaced method), or simplify the retry code so it uses only taught syntax, for example a comment stating "// equals now compares cents".

findings.claim: B1: feedback and check messages use "identity" ("compares identity like ==", "that tests identity, not text") and the hint uses "operands"; the Activity 4 teaching introduces "hashCode" and "that contract". None of these is defined on this page or an earlier one; the teaching says "same object", not "identity". The At work row says the == check "can pass in a quick test", but nothing on the page explains why == could ever pass for strings (identical literals sharing one object), so the line puzzles a learner who just saw it print false.
findings.recommendation: Replace "identity" with "whether both refer to the same object" (or define it once in Activity 2), say "the two values being compared" for operands, drop or gloss "contract", and either add a clause that two identical literals in source code share one object or rephrase the At work row without that claim.

findings.claim: G4/A2: the decision is "Compare with == or with equals?", but the next row starts "Use it when", so the learner cannot tell which of the two "it" is. The boundary row then answers with ==, which implies "it" is equals, but a beginner must infer that.
findings.recommendation: Name the choice in the row: "Use equals when: you test whether two objects hold the same content, such as two strings."

findings.claim: D5: hint 2 for Activity 3 ("Replace the == operator with a call to the comparison method from the teaching, made on one string with the other as its argument") is the finished expression written as prose; together with the teaching example it leaves no reasoning step.
findings.recommendation: Make hint 2 a reasoning step, for example "Look at the teaching's answer.equals("yes") line: which word in it is the method, and which string plays the role of answer in your condition?"

findings.claim: A4: the interview probe "what is the difference between == and equals?" is exactly what Activity 2 practises, but the page does not say so.
findings.recommendation: Append "Activity 2 practises exactly this." (or similar) to the In interviews row.

findings.claim: Other real problem (E1/F5): the practice editor does not check statements inside method or constructor bodies. Exercised at 570 px: Menu.java with "if (input.equals("quit") {" (missing ")") or "return "bye"" (missing ";") is accepted. The Problems tab says "No problems found in the parts this editor reads" and feedback says "All 5 checks pass", while other syntax errors on the same page are reported as "the compiler would reject this code". A beginner reads the pass as "this compiles" and learns that the missing semicolon or bracket is fine. Overlaps the SME fidelity review.
findings.recommendation: Either have the parser require a terminating ";" and balanced parentheses on body statements, reporting them through the existing "Not checked ... does not count as a try" path, or state beside Check code that statement punctuation inside methods is not checked, so the pass is not read as "compiles".

location.selector: #activity-3 #fb-3 (inline engine: second checked try, verdict set)

findings.claim: E3 (practice-feedback-policy 1.1): a near-miss is only treated as one on the first checked try ("Almost: ..."). On the second (last) checked try the same one-detail miss leads with the failure verdict "Not this time: N-1 of N checks pass after your second checked try" (observed for a one-check miss such as input.equalsIgnoreCase("help")), and the activity is closed for credit. The policy says a near-miss never gets a failure verdict.
findings.recommendation: When exactly one check fails on the last checked try, lead with the near-miss verdict ("Almost: ...") and the specific nudge, in pep-verdict--near styling, then state that the result is recorded and practice can continue.

findings.claim: B5/G1: the completion summary names activities by internal labels ("True or false", "Fix comparisons", "Final check") that match none of the lesson-path row titles the learner has seen ("Predict true or false", "Fix a menu that compares with ==", "Compare objects of your own class"). A learner told "Final check: answered, not yet correct" has to guess which activity that is.
findings.recommendation: Make each PEP_PAGE label equal to its lesson-path row title, or have the completion summary read the row title.

findings.claim: B2/GIFT: the item asks which declaration overrides equals and explains the distractors with "a Point parameter makes a new overload" and "without public it narrows the inherited access, which the compiler rejects". The page never teaches the equals signature, overload-versus-override (taught in inheritance-and-design, the next module) or the access-narrowing rule, so the item tests material the learner has not met rather than retention.
findings.recommendation: Replace it with an o3 item answerable from the page, for example predicting x.equals(y) for a class with and without an override in a new context, or move the signature question to the polymorphism topic.

findings.claim: B1/GIFT: the feedback "Reading methods such as nextLine do not add a trailing space" names nextLine, which no earlier java-foundations page or this page teaches, so the explanation leans on an unexplained API name.
findings.recommendation: Say "Reading a typed line does not add a trailing space" without naming nextLine.

location.selector: h2 "Cheat sheet" and h2 "Static interaction alternatives"

findings.claim: Other real problem (companion): the Markdown companion files every hint, the optional anecdote or challenge text under the "Cheat sheet" heading, repeats the summary text ("Another hint Another hint, 2 of 2 for Activity 3"), titles the static alternatives with engine type names ("predict", "drag", "explore", "mcq"; the lane activity is not dragged), and omits the On the job card with its At work and In interviews rows. The same generator output appears on all 255 topics, so this is a tooling defect rather than this page's authoring.
findings.recommendation: Raise a tooling-branch fix: give hints, anecdote and challenge their own headings, use activity titles instead of interaction types, de-duplicate summary text and carry the On the job card. No page-level change needed in this module branch.
